### Step 1 — Scene
A mixed dinner plate with yellow couscous-like grains, grilled meat strips (likely beef), a Caesar-style salad, and cooked squash/zucchini.

### Step 2 — Vessel
A rounded-square dinner plate, approximately **26 cm across**. Using the requested circular approximation:
**Area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ 531 cm².**

### Steps 3–7 — Items, area, volume, weight, and energy
The salad includes visible creamy dressing and grated cheese. These are included in its weight and energy estimate rather than counted twice. Croutons are separate.

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Bulk density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Yellow seasoned couscous | 23% | 122 cm² × 1.8 cm = 220 ml | 0.8 g/ml | 176 g | 150 | 264 kcal |
| Grilled beef strips | 13% | 69 cm² × 1.3 cm = 90 ml | 0.95 g/ml | 85 g | 240 | 204 kcal |
| Romaine with creamy dressing and grated cheese | 24% | 127 cm² × 2.5 cm = 318 ml | 0.2 g/ml | 64 g | 130 | 83 kcal |
| Cooked yellow squash, zucchini, and pale vegetable pieces | 13% | 69 cm² × 2 cm = 138 ml | 0.6 g/ml | 83 g | 45 | 37 kcal |
| Croutons | 4% | 21 cm² × 1.7 cm = 36 ml | 0.3 g/ml | 11 g | 410 | 45 kcal |

**Coverage check:** 23 + 13 + 24 + 13 + 4 = **77%**, consistent with the visible food and exposed plate rim.

### Step 8 — Sanity check
The estimate totals **419 g and approximately 633 kcal**. This is plausible for the visible grain mound, several meat strips, vegetables, and a leafy salad. Dressing quantity, meat cut, and grain preparation are the largest uncertainties.
